title: Hispano-Mozarabic manuscript witnesses, printed transmission and modern critical reform

traditions.label: Old Hispanic manuscript witnesses; recension unassigned
traditions.scope: Identified medieval witnesses whose exact A/B classification has not been established in this dossier.
traditions.coverage_note: The British Library witness is fragmentary and composite. Its geographic origin does not by itself establish a recension or ancestry for the printed missal.

traditions.label: Hispanic manuscript tradition A
traditions.scope: The manuscript tradition represented, in the 1988 Praenotanda, by most northern witnesses and the Santa Eulalia scriptorium at Toledo.
traditions.coverage_note: Distinct from B, especially in reading arrangements and parts of the Mass structure. No individually collated A manuscript stage is yet admitted here. The Praenotanda attribution to Julian of Toledo is an historical hypothesis, not an independently dated stage.

traditions.label: Tradition B and its Toledan printed transmission
traditions.scope: The Saints Justa and Rufina manuscript tradition as represented through the 1500 printed compilation and its later editions.
traditions.coverage_note: B is not a corrupt form of A. The 1500 compilation transmits B through editorial work and Roman devotional additions; many manuscript exemplars used by its editors are lost. The print is not an intact seventh-century missal.

traditions.label: Modern Hispano-Mozarabic critical corpus
traditions.scope: Modern missal and complementary lectionary assembled from both manuscript traditions for Catholic Hispano-Mozarabic worship.
traditions.coverage_note: The 1991 Temporal and 1994 complementary volume form one missal corpus. Approval dates, separate Order volumes and Liber Commicus publications do not create successive replacements of the whole missal.

sources.title: British Library, Add MS 30846: two incomplete copies of the Liber misticus
sources.inspection: Read complete institutional description, dates, contents, interleaved folio groups, provenance and bibliography. No manuscript images or complete transcription acquired.
sources.limitations: Catalogue establishes a composite witness and approximate date, not textual collation or an A/B classification.

sources.title: Missale mixtum secundum regulam beati Isidori dictum Mozarabes; Alexander Lesley, Rome 1755
sources.inspection: Acquired complete 761-page Florence/Google PDF. Image-inspected title (PDF 8), Advent IV pp 15–16 (PDF 134–135), Benedictio panis p 471 (PDF 591), reprinted 1500 colophon (PDF 592), Appendix prima p 621 (PDF 739). Other pages searched only as OCR leads. On 2026-10-19 the exact original JPEG2000 source image 590 was retained and independently collated against the complete nineteen-line Benedictio panis transcription (nine units); it resolves quinque where the bilevel PDF obscures i. Title PDF 8, publisher dedication and reprinted colophon PDF 592 were reopened. On 2026-10-20 the publisher dedication (PDF 15) and Lesley Preface III–IV, sections 15–19 (PDF 26–27), were directly image-read and independently reviewed: Lesley explicitly uses two parchment copies of Toledo 1500 and names the terminal bread blessing. This supports only the separately authorized complete-constituent edition republication, not a particular physical donor or whole-book textual collation. On 2026-10-21 printed p. 16, column a, lines 22-24 (PDF 135) was re-read at enlargement for the Memento/Creed rubric before Summe summe.
sources.limitations: Complete file acquisition is not complete transcription or complete page review. Native bindings cover only the complete Benedictio panis and the Ordo core on pp. 5-6. NYPL’s 408-image copy is incomplete and was not substituted for the complete Florence copy; only its title leaf and pp. 5-6 are retained, for the Ordo core. The original 1500 colophon is now separately retained and inspected in the Castilla-La Mancha witness. The retained Florence PDF page 135 is a 72 ppi bilevel derivative; the p. 16 rubric is legible only at enlargement, and the original JPEG2000 for that page could not be re-fetched while archive.org was unreachable on 2026-10-21. Cold review 2026-10-21: printed p. 16 was re-read from archive.org page image n134 (685×937 greyscale, SHA-256 5ea1685ea1b247236bcd4a0a28086a6daf7c6e8f10aabead1e4d53fa76158fa8), confirming the column-a rubric; the IIIF full-size request returned HTTP 504.

sources.title: Missale Gothicum, Rome: Fulgonius, 1804; BSB Res/2 Liturg. 222 m
sources.inspection: Inspected BSB IIIF manifest (854 canvases), title canvas 7; water blessing p XV and bread blessing p XVI (canvases 21–22); Temporal cols 1–2 (canvas 23), Advent IV cols 39–40 (canvas 42); Arévalo Illustratio cols 1145–1146 and Lesley dissertation cols 1147–1148 (canvases 667–668). The title and complete bread blessing were freshly reopened on 2026-10-19; all nineteen transcription lines and nine semantic units were independently collated. The reprinted colophon (canvas 666) and editor’s method (canvas 667) are now retained canonically and independently reviewed; the colophon repeats 1755’s Bagembach error against the original 1500 Hagenbach. Whole-book regeneration succeeded on 2026-10-19: HEAD 200 and GET bytes 0–31 returned 206, application/pdf and total 744082515 bytes. A subsequent complete GET acquired all 744082515 bytes; independently verified SHA-256 c5eb4c0dc348d13aab77b35b4232c0c74c2a162a475bfbdca33c4362841784f9. PDF inspection established 855 pages: a modern BSB delivery cover plus 854 book images. Complete image census found one scan image on each PDF page 2–855; cover, first two book images and canvas 22 at PDF page 23 were visually checked. On 2026-10-21 the full-resolution canvas 42 image (cols 39-40) was freshly fetched from the BSB IIIF image service (1407765 bytes, SHA-256 0eb7becf3c733796d2936afa00199376f9ba58626a2a106baba31db4760e6803) and col 40 read completely.
sources.limitations: The complete 855-page PDF (delivery cover plus 854 book images) was acquired and hashed, but remains deliberately remote because its measured 744082515-byte size would substantially increase every ordinary-Git checkout; the exact reason and retrieval receipt are in the canonical bsb-complete-pdf artifacts. Generated links expire; the institutional whole-book form can regenerate them. Exact retained title, complete blessing, Ordo core (canvases 28-31), colophon and editorial-method pages support the bounded offline claims. Remaining pages are not available in an offline checkout; no complete-volume collation is claimed. BSB NoC-NC/1.0 conditions remain explicit for hosted images and PDF.

sources.title: Jordi Pinell, Missale Hispano-Mozarabicum, decree and Praenotanda; Notitiae 24 (1988), 670–727
sources.inspection: Acquired entire official issue. Image-inspected pp 670–672, 678–679, 710–711, 721–724 and 729: editorial introduction, signed interim confirmation, manuscript traditions, order of Creed/fraction, composition and changes, decree summary.

sources.title: Notitiae 30 (1994), 544: individual faculties to celebrate in the Hispano-Mozarabic rite
sources.inspection: Complete official issue acquired 2026-10-21 (1915025 bytes, SHA-256 3c9ee227ebef4d00d5f50102f203903f5b5e63217b31a11f2e080daa6e70990e); printed p. 544 (PDF 32) read on the page image. sources.title: Jesús Camarero Cuñado, La figura del santo en la liturgia: fuentes archivísticas, Memoria Ecclesiae 24 (2004)
sources.inspection: Complete publisher/institutional volume downloaded; printed pp. 688–689/PDF 688–689 visually inspected. Explicitly identifies Toledo 35.3 as tradition A, describes 234 folios and 12th-century Santa Eulalia copying.
sources.limitations: Original scholarly discussion, not a direct manuscript facsimile or a modern final-missal collation. Dating differs materially from Férotin 1912; neither a 1912 manuscript date nor a common A/B ancestor is inferred.

sources.title: Missale mixtum, Toledo 1500; Biblioteca de Castilla-La Mancha Inc.1, record 12134
sources.inspection: All 973 offered institutional image positions were acquired and retained as ten lossless PDF parts with exact per-page URL/hash receipts. sources.title: Notitiae 28 (1992), no. 311: editorial Riti nella Chiesa (p. 365), Summarium decretorum (p. 396) and report of the papal Mass in the Hispano-Mozarabic rite (p. 404)
sources.inspection: Complete official issue acquired 2026-10-22 (6,206,072 bytes, SHA-256 9c446cdd8ba3c2ccd55874509d099964fb42091c67eaa696f2205c6561bcb1b9); PDF 3, 34 and 42 (printed pp. 365, 396, 404) read as page images. stages.label: Toledo 35.3: tradition A sacramentary
stages.date_label: Medieval; 12th century in 2004 study, 9th century in Férotin 1912
stages.scope: Individually identified priestly euchology witness, mediated by a critical edition and later scholarship; exact manuscript date remains unresolved.
stages.witness_label: Toledo Cathedral Library 35.3, 234 folios; Santa Eulalia ownership; chief witness of Férotin 1912.
stages.summary: Tradition A is now represented by an identified manuscript witness, without a false A→B succession.

evidence.claim: Explicitly assigns 35.3 toA and describes its variable priestly prayers and lacunae.
Describes lost first leaves, 234 folios, two hands and Santa Eulalia provenance; distinguishes the manuscript from the 1912 supplemented critical edition.

stages.limitations: No direct 35.3 images acquired. Date bounds deliberately unset because inspected sources disagree. 1912 publication is not the date of this manuscript; Férotin supplements its lacunae from other manuscripts, so the complete edition must not be labeled pure 35.3. Exact contributions to 1991/1994 remain uncollated.
stages.reception: Evidence of a medieval Hispanic source tradition, later used in critical reconstruction; no continuous or exclusive modern reception inferred.

stages.label: Fragmentary Old Hispanic Mass and Office books
stages.scope: Two interleaved incomplete Libri mistici, Easter through Pentecost; not a complete annual missal.
stages.summary: The two-column manuscript occupies ff 1–6, 25–56, 75–87; the single-column manuscript ff 7–24, 57–74, 88–175. The catalogue records numerous gaps, a reused passionary fragment at f 173 and an incomplete later addition of northern Visigothic neumes.

evidence.claim: Identifies two incomplete Mass/Office manuscripts, c 1000, and their present interleaving.

stages.limitations: Catalogue-based state; no exact A/B assignment, full reading cycle reconstruction, chant realization or descendant claim. The bounds date the manuscripts rather than the duration of rite use.
stages.reception: Historical Old Hispanic liturgical witness associated with the Burgos/Silos region; neither its survival nor provenance establishes a modern Catholic reception decree.

stages.label: Cisneros’s printed Toledan missal
stages.scope: Latin printed Mass book compiling the Toledan B tradition under Alfonso Ortiz; whole-book identity, with order evidence supplied by official retrospectives.
stages.witness_label: Missale mixtum secundum regulam beati Isidori dictum Mozarabes; Toledo 1500
stages.summary: The print consolidates B-based materials used by the Saints Justa and Rufina community. Its Order retains Creed before fraction and Lord’s Prayer, while adding Roman devotional material to Hispanic formulas. The printed compilation is an editorial state with partly lost manuscript exemplars.

evidence.claim: Distinguishes A/B; attributes printed books to B; names the 1500 missal and its retained Creed/fraction sequence.

evidence.locus: Unnumbered reprinted colophon after p 471, PDF 592
evidence.claim: Reprints the completion date 9 January 1500, Toledo printer and Ortiz’s role.
Describes the 1500 Ordo as Hispanic formulas adapted to a Roman Toledan order with priestly apologies.
Traces the Roman-Toledan preparatory layer and composite Hispanic Order, including Toledo 35.6; attributes the James formulary to Toledo 35.3 and London Add.30844.

evidence.locus: Position 964, complete blessing; position 965, original publication colophon
evidence.claim: Complete source-defined Benedictio panis independently image-collated and bound as nine native text units, with declared reading normalization; no complete Ordinary or missal claimed.

evidence.locus: Positions 31-34, ff. v r - vi v (Dominica prima de adventu)
evidence.claim: Ordo core from the rubric before Adesto through the Liberati embolism, including the two variable Advent I prayers printed inside it (post pridie; ad orationem dominicam), independently image-collated and bound as twenty native text units with declared reading normalization; no complete Ordinary or missal claimed.

stages.limitations: Exact 9 January 1500 publication date is directly inspected in the original colophon, in addition to its 1755 reprint. All 973 offered image positions are retained, but the full book has not been transcribed or collated and physical completeness is not independently established. Native text bindings cover only the complete bread blessing and the Ordo core printed in Dominica prima de adventu (positions 31-34), including its two variable Advent I prayers. The Roman-source dating differs in emphasis between 1988 (thirteenth-century copies) and 2014 (fifteenth-century usage); no false reconciliation.
stages.reception: Cisneros established the Corpus Christi chapel for daily Mass and Office; the 1988 account also notes earlier parish use. No claim that every manuscript or parish followed this printed recension.

stages.label: Lesley’s annotated republication
stages.scope: Republication with extensive historical preface, explanatory notes and appendices; representative liturgical pages and terminal blessing checked.
stages.witness_label: Missale mixtum, Alexander Lesley; Rome, Monaldini / typis Joannis Generosi Salomoni, 1755
stages.summary: Lesley gives the inherited printed missal a scholarly apparatus. The inspected body includes Advent IV’s variable euchology and blessing; Benedictio panis stands at p 471 before the original colophon and later notes. Appendix prima prints a Mass attributed to St Pelagius from Sandoval; an appendix is not automatically part of the prescribed liturgical body.

evidence.claim: Identifies edition, sampled Mass body, terminal bread blessing and scholarly appendix.
Calls 1755 a re-edition with Lesley’s presentation and explanatory notes; identifies PL 85 as a reproduction of it.

evidence.locus: Printed p. 471, original source image 590 / PDF page 591
evidence.claim: Complete source-defined Benedictio panis independently image-collated and bound as nine native text units, with declared reading normalization; no complete Ordinary or missal claimed.

evidence.locus: Printed pp. 5-6 (NYPL/Google copy images 0127-0128; Florence image 0123 for the marginal note)
evidence.claim: Ordo core from the rubric before Adesto through the Liberati embolism, including the two variable Advent I prayers printed inside it (post pridie; ad orationem dominicam), independently image-collated and bound as twenty native text units with declared reading normalization; Lesley's line numbers excluded; no complete Ordinary or missal claimed.

stages.limitations: No whole-body 1500/1755 collation or substantive ritual revision is claimed. The entire offered Florence PDF is retained; only the complete nine-unit Benedictio panis, using the sharper original JPEG2000 page, and the Ordo core printed in Dominica prima de adventu (pp. 5-6) are bound as native text. The Ordo core is read from the NYPL digitization of the same edition, whose full-resolution pages are legible where the Florence images are 685 pixels wide; only its gutter-cropped marginal note is read on the Florence page. Comparison preserves the presbiter/presbyter orthographic difference without treating it as a new prayer version.
stages.reception: A scholarly republication of the Toledan printed tradition. Its publication alone does not demonstrate substitution in every celebrating community.

stages.label: Lorenzana–Arévalo corrected missal
stages.scope: Corrected edition of the inherited printed missal, with relocated blessing and reused/augmented scholarly apparatus.
stages.witness_label: Missale Gothicum secundum regulam beati Isidori hispalensis episcopi; Rome, Fulgonius 1804; BSB bsb 10869679
stages.summary: Arévalo completed Lorenzana’s posthumous edition. The title calls it recognized and reprinted; Arévalo explains his reuse of Lesley’s dissertation and notes, addition of his own notes and attempted correction of faulty or obscure readings, with further manuscript collation left to readers who had access. Benedictio panis now precedes the Temporal at p XVI.

evidence.locus: Title canvas 7; p XVI canvas 22; cols 1145–1148 canvases 667–668
evidence.claim: Directly establishes imprint, moved blessing and editor’s account of relation to 1755.
Calls 1804 a corrected edition and reports it as the book then in use for daily Toledo chapel celebration.

evidence.locus: Printed p. XVI, right column, BSB canvas 22
evidence.claim: Complete source-defined Benedictio panis independently image-collated and bound as nine native text units, with declared reading normalization; no complete Ordinary or missal claimed.

evidence.locus: Printed cols. 12-17, BSB canvases 28-31 (Dominica prima de adventu)
evidence.claim: Ordo core from the rubric before Adesto through the Liberati embolism, including the two variable Advent I prayers printed inside it (post pridie; ad orationem dominicam), independently image-collated and bound as twenty native text units with declared reading normalization; no complete Ordinary or missal claimed.

stages.limitations: Exact selected pages, the complete nine-unit bread blessing and the Ordo core printed in Dominica prima de adventu (cols. 12-17) are checked; the acquired and hashed 744082515-byte complete PDF remains remote for its measured size. No full-lineage or exhaustive text-change count is claimed. Do not confuse this edition with PL 85’s 1862 reprint of 1755. Edition dependence and changed blessing placement do not by themselves identify the immediate textual parent of this constituent.
stages.reception: Contemporary 1988 reform introduction reports daily use of the 1804 book in Toledo’s Mozarabic chapel. This attests use in 1988; it does not establish a universal 1804 effective date or uninterrupted use everywhere.

stages.label: Critical missal incorporating both traditions
stages.scope: Completed complementary Latin missal corpus, positioned at the second tome’s 1994 publication; first tome published in 1991. Calendar, revised Order, Temporal, saints’ Proper/Common, deceased and votive Masses; readings and chants drawn from both traditions.
stages.witness_label: Missale Hispano-Mozarabicum, CEE / Archdiocese of Toledo, 1991 and 1994
stages.summary: The reform retains B’s Creed–fraction–Lord’s Prayer order but reconstructs the Order with A evidence, removes inherited Roman devotional additions and supplies optional quiet prayers from the Hispanic Liber ordinum. Both traditions expand the readings, chant texts and euchology; selected celebrations have Year I/II variants, sometimes including Triduum structure. Latin readings use the Neovulgate.

evidence.claim: Defines the corpus and concrete reform operations.
17 July 1988 is interim confirmation of Praenotanda, Order and Temporal pending remaining parts; not a complete-missal publication date.
Records 1994 missal and 23 January 1994 confirmation, Prot 203/86 and CD 763/92.

evidence.locus: Paragraph beginning Ancora disponibile solo in latino
evidence.claim: Explicitly identifies first volume 1991 and second 1994.
Describes commission changes and final confirmation.
Official decree summary: Latin text of the Missale Hispano-Mozarabicum approved for Spain, 23 January 1994, Prot. CD 763/92.
Three personal faculties of 5 October 1994 (Prot. 857/94/L, 861/94/L, 862/94/L) for named priests to celebrate Mass in the Hispano-Mozarabic rite; grants, not attested celebrations.

The first part of the Missal (de tempore), confirmed 17 July 1988, was promulgated and entered into force; printing of the new book was completed in 1991 and its use extended to Spanish places requesting it.
A Latin Christmas Oratio admonitionis is cited from Missale Hispano-Mozarabicum, Toledo 1991.

stages.limitations: No protected modern full book was acquired or transcribed. Change evidence is primary-description, not line-by-line collation. The 1988 design envisaged a separate Order volume; exact final binding and every volume table of contents remain uninspected. The two publication years are not two replacement editions. Notitiae 29 (1993) p. 726 lists Missale Hispano-Mozarabicum and Liber Commicus (Conferencia Episcopal Española, Arzobispado de Toledo, Coeditores Litúrgicos, Barcelona 1991) under the 17 July 1988 confirmation with the language field 'hispanica'; whether that field denotes Spanish-language volumes or misdescribes the Latin books is not established, and the notice supplies no title-leaf data.
stages.reception: Prepared for living Catholic Hispano-Mozarabic communities. The 1988 introduction names Toledo chapel/parish context; no present-day universal permission or precise effective date is inferred from bibliographical notices. Notitiae 30 (1994) p. 544 records three personal faculties of 5 October 1994 to celebrate Mass in the Hispano-Mozarabic rite, granted to a diocesan priest of Mallorca, a Claretian and a Piarist (Prot. 857/94/L, 861/94/L and 862/94/L); the grants name no place of celebration and are not attested celebrations. On 28 May 1992 John Paul II celebrated Mass in this rite in the Vatican Basilica (Notitiae 28 (1992) p. 404), and on 28 December 1993 a further personal faculty was granted to Pere Farnés Scherer of Barcelona (Prot. 2441/93/L, Notitiae 29 (1993) p. 688). These are single celebrations or grants, not evidence of general use.

stages.label: Complementary saints readings volume
stages.scope: The saints-volume witness of the Liber Commicus companion to the reformed missal; part of a two-volume reading corpus, not a successor missal.
stages.witness_label: Liber Commicus (Missale Hispano-Mozarabicum); Proprium de Sanctis, Toledo 1995
stages.summary: The separately published lectionary supplies the reading component of the same reform. This stage dates the directly verified 1995 Latin saints-volume witness; the official 1996 notice reports 23 January 1994 confirmation.

evidence.claim: Names the 1995 Proprium de Sanctis companion and confirmation date.
Identifies Missale and Liber Commicus as paired products of the commission, each in two volumes.

stages.limitations: Only 1995 saints-volume imprint is directly verified here. The existing catalogue’s 1994 Temporal year awaits its own title-page check; 2014’s broad 1991–1994 summary must not erase the specific 1995 record. No full modern text acquired.
stages.reception: Companion book of the Catholic Hispano-Mozarabic reform. Separate publication and shared confirmation do not establish a new whole-missal revision or autonomous rite.

transitions.summary: The 1500 printed missal is republished with Lesley’s historical introduction, explanatory notes and appendices. No substantive rewriting of its liturgical body is established by this dossier.

changes.before: The 1500 printed corpus as identified by the later edition and official account.
changes.after: A later witness presents the inherited corpus with explanatory apparatus and an explicitly separate Appendix prima containing a St Pelagius Mass; appendix status is preserved.

evidence.claim: The book identifies its relation to the earlier print and visibly distinguishes apparatus/appendix from liturgical body.
Describes 1755 as re-edition plus preface and explanatory notes.
Explicit relationship of 1500 and 1755 editions.
1500 Advent IV rubric before Summe summe directly read: Et dicto memento pro viuis et perfecto simbolo dicat presbyter orationem dominicam, ending with an abbreviated adverb read as equaliter.
The same rubric in expanded spelling, ending equaliter.

transitions.limitations: This is a transmission/apparatus edge, not evidence of a new liturgical recension. No full 1500/1755 collation, no new mandatory formulary inferred from scholarly appendices. The complete bread blessing is now independently collated in both witnesses. Its unchanged lexical content with presbiter/presbyter spelling does not establish a new liturgical version or authorize native Git ancestry. The Advent IV Memento/Creed rubric (1500 f. XVIr col a; 1755 p. 16 col a) agrees in wording apart from abbreviation and spelling, read from a low-resolution 1755 derivative; this is one further bounded unit, not a body collation.

transitions.summary: The complete bread blessing moves from the end of the 1755 liturgical body to the 1804 preliminaries before the Temporal, its words agreeing after declared spelling normalization; and in Advent IV the 1755 rubric directing the priest, after the Memento for the living and the Creed, to say the Lord's Prayer is replaced in 1804 by the heading Ad orationem Dominicam. Arévalo separately describes reusing and correcting Lesley's apparatus; edition dependence does not identify the immediate textual exemplar of either unit.

changes.before: Benedictio panis concludes the body at p 471, followed by the original 1500 colophon and explanatory material.
changes.after: Benedictio panis appears on p XVI after the water blessing, immediately before the Temporal opens at cols 1–2. The invocation, blessing prayer, Trinitarian blessing and sprinkling rubric remain present.
changes.locus_before: 1755 p 471, PDF 591 and following colophon PDF 592

evidence.claim: Direct page reading establishes terminal placement and the full blessing sequence.
Direct page reading establishes relocation to preliminaries and retained sequence.

changes.before: After the post-pridie prayer: Et dicto memento pro vivis et perfecto symbolo dicat Presbyter orationem Dominicam equaliter, as in the 1500 print (f. XVIr col a).
changes.after: The same place carries only the red heading Ad orationem Dominicam before Summe, summe, et omnipotens Deus; the following Pater noster and blessing rubric is unchanged in substance.
changes.locus_before: 1755 p. 16 col a, lines 22-24, PDF 135; 1500 position 53, f. XVIr col a

evidence.claim: Long rubric read at enlargement.
The 1500 form of the long rubric directly read.
Replacement heading directly read.
Cites col 40 against 1500 f. XVIra as an example of small rubric modifications.
Arévalo describes dependence on Lesley, addition of notes and corrections, while further manuscript collation is left to readers with access.
Independent study identifies modest corrections and bread-blessing relocation.

evidence.locus: Publisher dedication PDF 15; Lesley Preface III–IV §§15–19, PDF 26–27
evidence.claim: Separate exact-constituent evidence supports 1500-edition republication in 1755; it does not authorize an immediate 1755-to-1804 native parent.

transitions.limitations: The text-collated claim is bounded to this blessing and placement, not a complete-edition collation or substantial ritual reform. Correction (2026-10-21, new evidence): the earlier statement that the Advent IV rubric at 1804 col 40 already matches 1755 p 16 is true of the Pater noster and blessing rubric but not of the Memento/Creed rubric, which 1755 keeps in its 1500 form and 1804 replaces with a heading; the 1755 reading rests on a 72 ppi derivative. No exact count of corrections. Separate primary evidence authorizes a 1500-edition republication parent for the complete 1755 blessing; the 1804 snapshot remains an isolated root. Same-prayer comparison, printed placement and the edition’s reuse of Lesley do not establish a substantive prayer revision or an immediate 1755→1804 constituent parent. Each snapshot materializes its own checked wording without text inheritance. The 1804 heading replaces a cross-referencing rubric within this Sunday's proper; the 1804 Order of Mass was not compared, so no change in whether or how the Memento for the living, the Creed or the Lord's Prayer is said is inferred. Cold review 2026-10-21 re-read 1755 p. 16 from the Internet Archive page image n134 (SHA-256 5ea1685ea1b247236bcd4a0a28086a6daf7c6e8f10aabead1e4d53fa76158fa8) and confirmed the reading.

transitions.summary: The inherited B-based printed missal is critically reconstructed using both Hispanic traditions: the Order’s devotional layer is revised, proper readings and chants expand into selected biennial cycles, Latin readings adopt the Neovulgate, and some formularies are adapted or omitted for contemporary use.

changes.before: The inherited printed Order combines B-based Hispanic formulas with Roman devotional additions introduced in the 1500 compilation.
changes.after: B remains the structural base while elements from A are incorporated and the Roman devotional additions are removed. Creed before fraction before Lord’s Prayer is expressly retained.
changes.locus_before: 1500 compilation continued by 1755/1804; described 1988 § 146 and 2014 p 506
changes.locus_after: 1988 § 146; § 117; 1991–1994 Order as described by its reform documents

evidence.claim: States both the reconstruction and the specific B-order continuity.
Explains the inherited hybrid Order and need for reconstruction.

changes.before: The inherited Order included devotional priestly prayers of Roman provenance.
changes.after: Three optional moments of quiet private prayer are permitted: opening, offertory and before Communion; texts are drawn from Hispanic votive Masses in the Liber ordinum.

evidence.claim: Identifies removal, optional replacement source, three positions and low-voice condition.

changes.before: The received printed missal principally transmitted the B tradition; A and B had distinct reading distributions.
changes.after: Selected Advent/Paschal Sundays and major feasts receive Year I/II reading cycles drawn from both traditions. Every Lenten Sunday and feria is assigned proper readings; all Latin readings adopt the Neovulgate.

evidence.claim: Gives inherited scope, new biennial design, Lenten provision and adopted Latin version.

changes.before: The older printed repertory represents B rather than the complete recovered A/B material.
changes.after: The reformed compilation gathers chant texts from both traditions; ordinary Year I/II variation runs from Praelegendum through Sacrificium. This does not reconstruct lost medieval melodies.

evidence.claim: Explicitly includes cantos in the expanded collection and defines normal scope of biennial variation.

changes.before: The received print offered the inherited B euchological repertory.
changes.after: Euchological material is gathered from both traditions. Normally Year I/II use the same prayers from Oratio Admonitionis onward, so the biennial cycle must not be represented as two universally different anaphoras.

evidence.claim: Defines expanded source repertory and continuity of the euchology after Oratio Admonitionis.

changes.before: Parallel A/B forms of the Triduum were not both represented by the received B-based printed line.
changes.after: The two-year Triduum can preserve structural differences as well as different readings and chants; it is more than a substitution of lections.

evidence.claim: Explicitly distinguishes structural variation in Holy Thursday, Good Friday and the Easter Vigil from ordinary biennial text variation.

changes.before: Old calendars sometimes commemorated saints for whom no corresponding proper Mass survived.
changes.after: The calendar is critically compared across Mozarabic/post-Mozarabic witnesses and offices/Mass lists; saints lacking a proper Mass use the Common.

evidence.claim: Describes critical-calendar method and the explicit response to missing propers.

changes.before: The inherited Common’s virgin formularies also referred to martyrdom; some needs formularies no longer suited the commission’s intended contemporary use.
changes.after: Virgin-only formularies were adapted by removing martyr references; some obsolete needs formularies were omitted. Individual formulae and omissions are not enumerated in the inspected account.
changes.locus_before: Source repertory described by commission account 2014 p 507

evidence.claim: Reports these concrete adaptation and omission operations.
Contemporary reform introduction distinguishes new all-source reconstruction from simple revision of 1804 and gives bounded changes.
Retrospective commission account corroborates Order reconstruction and formulary adaptation.

transitions.limitations: Primary-description establishes operations, not a full before/after transcription. No exact old/new formula text, exhaustive omission list, manuscript stemma, new chant melody or complete 1960s to 1990s promulgation history is inferred. Approval 17 July 1988 was partial; 1991/1994 volumes are complementary. Preservation of B Creed/fraction order is continuity, not an innovation.

gaps.missing: Direct manuscript images and current palaeographic resolution for the now individually identified tradition A witness Toledo 35.3; exact attribution of its contributions to the modern repertory.
gaps.next_source: Toledo Cathedral 35.3 original or complete institutional facsimile; compare Férotin 1912 xxv–xxvi, cols 689–690 with Camarero 2004 pp 688–689 and modern palaeography. Full 1912 PDF/OCR now retained canonically.
gaps.consequence: An explicit provisional A manuscript stage exists, with date bounds unset for the ninth-versus-twelfth-century disagreement. No common ancestor or A→B evolution edge is manufactured.

gaps.missing: Independent original verification of manuscript dependencies. Janini 1984 p 339 identifies Toledo 35.3 and London Add.30844 behind the James formulary, contradicting Férotin 1912 p xxvi on non-use of 35.3. This specific disagreement must be resolved before an exclusive B manuscript stemma is asserted.
gaps.next_source: Compare the James formulary in original 1500 with Toledo 35.3 and London Add.30844, using Janini 1984 pp 339–340 and Férotin 1912 p xxvi as competing critical accounts; check Toledo 35.6 institution narrative separately.
gaps.consequence: The printed line remains conventionally B-based; this classification does not establish exclusive dependence on B manuscripts or erase individual A-source contributions identified by later scholarship.

gaps.missing: Physical completeness review and complete-volume text collation of the retained 973-position 1500 sequence against the complete 1755 Florence witness. Bounded units now collated: the entire bread blessing and the Advent IV Memento/Creed rubric (f. XVIr col a against p. 16), which agree.
gaps.next_source: Retained Castilla-La Mancha positions (tracked parts 0001-0973) against a higher-resolution 1755 image source than the retained 72 ppi Florence derivative (the original JPEG2000 set, when archive.org is reachable), proceeding formulary by formulary from the Advent Sundays.
gaps.consequence: Original colophon directly establishes the exact 1500 date. Two units agree; no substantive 1500 to 1755 ritual revision is established or excluded.

gaps.missing: Full-volume text collation and exhaustive distinction between typographic corrections, apparatus changes and liturgical changes. Two bounded 1755 to 1804 rubric changes are now text-collated: the bread blessing relocation and the Advent IV Memento/Creed rubric replaced by Ad orationem Dominicam.
gaps.next_source: Regenerate the complete BSB bsb10869679 PDF (855 pages: delivery cover plus 854 book images) through its public whole-book form when a full-volume collation is undertaken. Canonical bsb-complete-pdf and retrieval metadata record the measured size and access limit; the complete blessing and editorial/colophon evidence already have retained exact images.
gaps.consequence: Bounded rubric changes are text-collated; the general correction claims and their number remain the editor's and Sierra Lopez's descriptions.

gaps.missing: Authorized complete final missal comparison, exact manuscript attribution of additions, individual virgin-text edits and omitted needs Masses.
gaps.next_source: Lawfully consulted Missale Hispano-Mozarabicum 1991/1994 title leaves, contents and changed loci; Pinell, El Misal Hispano-Mozárabe, nueva edición revisada, Phase 32 (1992), 367–380; commission 37 study documents referenced by Ramis 2014 p 507.
gaps.consequence: Concrete source-described reforms are documented, but no full modern text, exhaustive diff or authorization to retain protected books is claimed.

gaps.missing: Full text of the 23 January 1994 decree (Prot. CD 763/92), whose official summary is now inspected; directly inspected Temporal Liber Commicus imprint and final missal binding contents. The 203/88 versus 203/86 discrepancy is narrowed: the 1988 decree text itself prints no protocol, but cites the episcopal conference's petition of 18 December 1986, and the 1988 summary p. 729, the 1995 notice and the 1996 notice all give 203/86; only the editorial header p. 670 gives 203/88. Narrowed 2026-10-22: Notitiae 27–29 (1991–1993) were searched; they report the 1991 completion of printing and entry into force of the de tempore part (1992 pp. 365, 404) and cite a Latin prayer from Missale Hispano-Mozarabicum, Toledo 1991 (1991 p. 671), but print no Latin title-leaf data; their only bibliographical notice (1993 p. 726) lists Missale Hispano-Mozarabicum and Liber Commicus, Barcelona 1991, under the 1988 confirmation with the language field 'hispanica', so whether it notices the Latin tome or Spanish-language volumes is unresolved.
gaps.next_source: Title and decree leaves of the 1991/1994 Missale and 1994/1995 Liber Commicus; the title leaf and imprint of the Latin 1991 tome (Notitiae 1991-1993 now searched). Notitiae 30 (1994), all ten issues, were searched by OCR on 2026-10-21: only the p. 325 summary and the p. 544 faculties concern this rite.
gaps.consequence: Publication, confirmation and use are kept distinct. 203/86 is treated as the probable file number and 203/88 as an isolated header variant, without silently rewriting the 1988 record; no fabricated effective date or successive replacement edge between complementary volumes.
